questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'Don't count your chickens before they hatch.'

options.option_text: Raising chickens is a risky business.
Don't plan on the basis of something that has not yet happened.
Be patient while waiting for results.
Always plan ahead for future events.

questions.explanation: B is correct. This proverb warns against making plans or assuming results based on something uncertain. Example: You haven't been offered the job yet, so don't plan how to spend the salary — don't count your chickens before they hatch.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'A stitch in time saves nine.'

options.option_text: Sewing clothes is a time-saving skill.
Working slowly but steadily leads to better results.
Dealing with a problem early prevents it from becoming bigger later.
Nine is always better than one.

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'A stitch in time saves nine' = timely action prevents a small problem from growing into a larger one. Literally: one stitch made when a garment first tears will prevent needing nine stitches when the tear gets bigger. Example: Fix the leak today or it may flood the house next month.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'The pen is mightier than the sword.'

options.option_text: Pens are useful tools in modern warfare.
Education is more valuable than physical strength.
Swords are no longer used in modern conflicts.
Written words and ideas have more power and lasting influence than physical force.

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'The pen is mightier than the sword' = communication, literature, and ideas can bring about greater change than violence or military force. Written words can inspire revolutions, change laws, and shift public opinion in ways that weaponry cannot.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'Don't judge a book by its cover.'

options.option_text: Books should have attractive covers to sell well.
Avoid making judgments based solely on outward appearances.
Reading the preface of a book tells you all you need to know.
Publishers should invest more in book design.

questions.explanation: B is correct. This proverb advises against judging people or things solely based on their external appearance or first impression. Just as a book with a dull cover may contain rich content, a person who appears plain may have remarkable qualities.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'The early bird catches the worm.'

options.option_text: Birds that wake up early find more food.
Those who start earlier than others are more likely to succeed.
Worms are most active in the early morning.
Punctuality is the most important quality in life.

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'The early bird catches the worm' = starting a task or arriving early gives one a competitive advantage. Example: Applicants who submit resumes first often get interviews before the roles are filled.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'Every cloud has a silver lining.'

options.option_text: Meteorologists can predict rain from cloud formations.
Rainclouds reflect sunlight from below.
Every negative or difficult situation has some positive aspect or ray of hope.
Beautiful weather always follows a storm.

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Every cloud has a silver lining' = even in the most difficult times, there is some reason for hope or something positive to find. Origin: when clouds are backlit by the sun, their edges appear bright/silver despite the dark interior.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'Too many cooks spoil the broth.'

options.option_text: Professional kitchens require many skilled chefs.
Soup requires careful preparation.
Hiring too many people for a job is wasteful.
When too many people are involved in a task, the result is often poor.

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Too many cooks spoil the broth' = when too many people are involved in managing or deciding something, the outcome suffers due to conflicting ideas and lack of coordination. Example: The project failed because the committee had 15 members, each pushing a different direction.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'Actions speak louder than words.'

options.option_text: What you do is more meaningful and credible than what you say.
Loud people are more likely to take action.
Speaking confidently impresses people more than working quietly.
It is easier to talk about a problem than to solve it.

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Actions speak louder than words' = what a person actually does demonstrates their character and intent more clearly than what they say. Example: Don't say you care about the environment — take action by reducing your waste.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.'

options.option_text: Hunting is more rewarding than birdwatching.
It is better to be satisfied with what you have than to risk losing it for something uncertain.
Always grab opportunities before they disappear.
Two small gains are always better than one large gain.

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush' = a certain possession, even if modest, is more valuable than a larger but uncertain one. Example: Accept the job offer you have rather than gambling it away waiting for a potentially better (but uncertain) offer.

questions.stem:
What is the meaning of the proverb:
'Beggars can't be choosers.'

options.option_text: Poverty makes people desperate and immoral.
The poor should work harder to improve their own situation.
People who depend on the generosity of others should accept what they are given without complaints.
Helping others is always a choice, never an obligation.

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Beggars can't be choosers' = those who are in a position of need cannot afford to be selective about what they receive. If you need help, you should accept graciously what is offered rather than demanding something better.
